episode: Can a Harbour card pay a fare on a Northline ferry right now?

outline.name: The question
outline.description: Set up the trip, the card, and why the answer is not obvious.

outline.name: What was signed
outline.description: The January agreement, its scope, and the missing availability date.

outline.name: The disagreement
outline.description: The operator's live list against the trade report, both kept.

outline.name: What to do
outline.description: The fallback that works today, marked as the hosts' inference.

speakers.name: Ravi
speakers.voice_hint: brighter, faster, asks the blunt question

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: You are getting on a Northline ferry next month and you are holding a Harbour card. Does it work?

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.text: My instinct says yes, because I read that the two of them signed something in January.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Harbour Transit is not on Northline's live interoperability list, and a Harbour card cannot be used to pay a fare on a Northline service as of the twelfth of February 2026.

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.text: So what did they actually sign?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Northline Ferries and the Harbour Transit Authority signed a fare interoperability agreement on the third of January 2026.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: The signed agreement covers forty-two terminals across the two networks.

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.text: Forty-two terminals and no date. That is the part that tells you where this is.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Neither operator has announced a date for passenger availability.

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.text: But I did read that the deal enables Harbour cards on Northline. I am not making that up.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: You are not. Trade reporting describes the January 2026 agreement as enabling Harbour cards to be used for fare payment on Northline coastal services.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Both of those are in the ledger, both marked contested, because one is about what the agreement is for and the other is about what the reader will hit at the gangway.

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.text: And travellers have been finding out the hard way?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Travellers report Harbour cards being declined at the Northline gangway in December 2025 and again in February 2026.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: That one is marked reported rather than checked. A forum thread tells you what people hit. It does not tell you what the scheme supports.

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.text: So what do I do next month?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Paper tickets and cash remain available at every Northline terminal counter and at the quayside machines.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: The same travellers report that Meridian card taps work on the routes they used.

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.text: Cash, a paper ticket, or a Meridian Card. That is ours, not the sources'.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Recheck the operator's live list before you travel. It is the page every moving claim in this episode links to.
